blocks.text: Day 7 · After breakfast, a tour of one of Brazil’s most colourful cities, where African, Portuguese and Brazilian cultures blend. The African heritage, carried by the descendants of enslaved Africans, is especially felt in the cuisine and music; Salvador is famous for its carnival and festivals, and capoeira was born here. Explore the Lower City and visit the Church of Nosso Senhor do Bonfim, an 18th-century place of pilgrimage revered by Catholics and followers of Candomblé alike; climb up to the Monte Serrat fort for unique photos of the Bay of All Saints, and end at the Mercado Modelo craft market, perfect for souvenirs. Return to the hotel.

blocks.text: Day 8 · After breakfast, transfer to the airport and flight to Recife; transfer to the hotel. The capital of Pernambuco lies at the mouth of the Capibaribe River on the Atlantic, and is called the “Brazilian Venice” for its many canals and bridges. Despite its rapid growth, the city has kept traces of Portuguese and Dutch rule, with magnificent churches and historic mansions, beautiful beaches nearby, and many cafés, restaurants, shops and a lively nightlife.
